source.title: Temporal Calibrated Regularization for Robust Noisy Label Learning
source.authors: Dong-Xian Wu; Yisen Wang; Zhuobin Zheng; Shu-Tao Xia

record.tranche_reason: Tests learning under partially corrupted labels and reports that training accuracy may not approach 100% in the tested schedule; it does not test completely random labels or the full corruption sweep in V4.
record.gate_note: The paper studies uniform (symmetric) and asymmetric label noise, not completely random relabeling as in V1. It does not test V2, V3, V5, or V6. V4 is tested only partially: it evaluates several partial noise rates, and Figure 8 plots training and clean-test accuracy, but the text does not provide exact plotted values or test the full range through all labels corrupted. Table I reports clean-test accuracy by noise rate. Rows below capture its explicit Figure 8 statements and the CE and TCR scores from Table I for symmetric noise; asymmetric results are outside V4's stated random-corruption condition.
record.test_reason: The conventional cross-entropy baseline tests V4's test-error trend under partial uniform label corruption. The paper also reports its own learning trajectories supporting V6 in Figures 1 and 6, which the record overlooks. Its proposed noise-mitigation method does not establish a failure of ordinary networks to memorize labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that combining original labels with previous-epoch predictions and Squeeze improves robustness to noisy labels across tested datasets and architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Studies partially corrupted labels with a temporal label-correction method and Squeeze; it does not reproduce the original random-label experiment or its measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise rate changes clean-test accuracy; Figure 8 compares reflection loss with and without Squeeze. The paper states Squeeze significantly mitigates memorization of noisy samples under severe uniform noise.

fits_no_version.finding: TCR and its reflection-loss ablation improve noisy-label test accuracy; Squeeze reduces noisy-label memorization. The authors attribute slightly worse clean-data performance to their method resisting complete memorization within 150 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal label correction and prediction sharpening can mitigate memorization and improve generalization under noisy labels.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network
record.problems: No exact Figure 8 values are stated in the text. Training accuracy values are not given in Table I. The results use partial noise rates and do not test fully random labels or all labels corrupted. Table I reports averages over 5 runs but no error bars or other uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table I asymmetric-noise results were not included because V4 specifies randomly corrupted labels; the table's asymmetric noise conditions do not match that version. Other Table I methods were omitted to keep extraction focused on CE and the paper's TCR method. Figure 8 training and test plots are retained as figure-only rows because the text supplies no exact values.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling and near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparison between true and random labels, and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit at every corruption rate, the full sweep through completely random labels, and the chance-performance endpoint. CE test accuracies alone do not establish simultaneous signal learning and complete noise memorization.
Necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and ordinary data augmentation for memorization and generalization.
Population-level clean-versus-noisy learning rates and learning trajectories on completely random labels; Figure 6 provides illustrative sample trajectories rather than aggregate rates.

missing.what: Conventional CE sample trajectory: the incorrectly labeled airplane is initially learned according to its real pattern and later memorized according to its noisy label. Include the correctly labeled sample as the comparison; numerical probabilities cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
Architecture-specific onset of overfitting at 40% uniform noise on CIFAR-10: approximately epoch 30 for PreAct ResNet-18 and after epoch 80 for ResNet-32, within 150 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: The original limits_scope verdict confuses unmeasured parts of V4 with observed failures. The statement about training accuracy failing to approach 100% concerns the authors' mitigation method on clean data, not a demonstrated failure of conventional CE to fit randomly corrupted labels. Uniform noise here flips selected labels to other classes, with transition probabilities defined in Equation 6; the tested rates do not constitute completely random labeling.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labeling, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged training settings.
Relative training time and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Full sweep from no corruption to all labels corrupted; exact training-error results at each rate; whether the same model fits every condition perfectly.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Whether patterns in real data are learned before noisy or random labels.

relation.reason: The study reports its own baseline results bearing directly on test degradation with label noise and pattern learning before noisy-label memorization.

tranche.reason: Its conventional CE noise sweeps and learning trajectories test V4's degradation component and V6 through different experiments; the proposed mitigation does not establish a counterexample requiring T5.

source_check.notes: V6 trajectory evidence needs result rows; its absence from the rows does not invalidate the text-based verdict. Figure 8 concerns reflection loss with and without Squeeze, not conventional CE; the authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate.

statements.correction: PreAct ResNet-18, conventional CE, CIFAR-10; symmetric noise fractions 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6; clean-test accuracy 94.31%, 80.13%, 60.75%, 39.70%; averages over 5 runs; no standard deviations, confidence intervals or numerical uncertainty reported; perfect training fit not established for this sweep.
statements.problem: The PreAct ResNet-18 values, conditions and training-interpolation caveat are correct. The assertion of reported uncertainty overstates Table I, which supplies five-run means without dispersion or uncertainty estimates.
